name: MIRACL
listed_description: A Multiprecision Integer and Rational Arithmetic Cryptographic Library.
reason: The repo's docs/miracl-explained/benchmarks.md gives only absolute timings (e.g. 1024-bit RSA decryption 1.09 ms on a 2.4GHz Intel i5 520, GCC /O2; 233 MHz Pentium II tables) with no named baseline, and README/update.txt only say 'thoroughly optimised for speed' and 'up to 60% faster' versus its own earlier code (sse2.txt). A third-party study that reportedly has MIRACL best on binary-field (GF(2^m)) elliptic curves vs OpenSSL and others (GMU, cryptography.gmu.edu/publications/download.php?docid=956) and a 2019 ARES MIRACL/RELIC/WolfSSL paper are known only from search snippets; hosts blocked (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND). Repo licence is AGPL-3.0-or-later with a commercial option (README).

name: Newton Dynamics
listed_description: An integrated solution for real time simulation of physics environments.
reason: MADEAPPS repo README says it is discontinued in favour of JulioJerez/newton-dynamics; neither README, 'Newton Game Dynamics.md' nor the FAQ wiki has any number against PhysX, Bullet or ODE. Only comparisons found are a 2017 Leadwerks forum thread (leadwerks.com unreachable, getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND) where the author posted graphs vs PhysX 3.4 and Bullet 2.85 and, per search snippets, described Newton as marginally slower than PhysX; disputed and not a repo benchmark. Guessed category blas-lapack was wrong (physics engine). zlib licence.

name: ofxBox2d
reason: Thin openFrameworks wrapper around Box2D v2.3; README has no performance claim, and the example-Performance folder is an app with no README or numbers. Any speed result would belong to Box2D itself.

name: PARI/GP
listed_description: Computer algebra system for number theory; includes a
reason: No numbers reachable. pari.math.u-bordeaux.fr/benchs.html is unreachable (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND); no official GitHub mirror (github.com/pari-gp/pari is 404). Leads from search results only (pages unreachable): mpfr.org/mpfr-2.3.0/timings.html 100-digit table (search summary: PARI multiplication about 0.00017 ms vs Magma about 0.0006 ms and Mathematica about 0.0015 ms, circa 2007 hardware); arXiv 2002.04717 'Computing classical modular forms' (PARI/GP vs Magma totals, summary garbled); flintlib.org/benchmarks.html (unreachable) reportedly shows PARI/GP 2.5.4 losing to Magma at degree 3000 polynomial factoring. Guessed category fft was wrong (number theory CAS).

name: PETSc
listed_description: Suite of data structures and routines for scalable parallel
reason: Repo (gitlab.com/petsc/petsc, GitHub mirror petsc/petsc, BSD-2-Clause) docs checked: doc/manual/performance.md, doc/faq/index.md, doc/index.md have only PETSc-vs-PETSc speedup and tuning advice, no named-baseline numbers. Comparisons live in papers (e.g. arXiv 1607.00351 PETSc Krylov vs hypre BoomerAMG and Trilinos ML, PETSc 3.7.1; arXiv 1705.03625) which are blocked here. FiPy's SOLVERS.rst compares solver suites only as plots without numbers. Guessed category fft was wrong (the fit is sparse-and-solvers).
